ledger.note: 534: the Northern Wei splits and Yuwen Tai rules the west. Infobox 'Establishment of Eastern Wei, start of division of Northern Wei: 8 November 534' and 'Emperor Wen's ascension, often viewed as establishment: 18 February 535'; 'it ruled the western part of northern China from 535 to 557 AD'. The year-month is the division's; the Yuwen Tai page has Emperor Xiaowu fleeing west in fall 534 and being poisoned around the new year 535.

union.text: the western Henan and southwestern Shanxi lands of the Western Wei shape

region.text: the Luoyang region and the Henan-Shanxi lands west of it, the zone the Eastern Wei dossier fights over in 537-538

ledger.note: 537: Yuwen Tai attacks the Eastern Wei. 'In fall 537, Yuwen led an attack on Eastern Wei and captured Hengnong'; the Eastern Wei counter-attack, Shayuan, is the page's only named battle (Western Wei page: 'withstood Eastern Wei attacks there').

537: the Western Wei hold the Luoyang region. The Yuwen Tai page has only 'In fall 537, Yuwen led an attack on Eastern Wei and captured Hengnong'; the Eastern Wei dossier (Gao Huan page) has the Western Wei taking the Luoyang region in 537. Bridged so the loss booked there has an owner.
538: the Western Wei leave the Luoyang region. The Yuwen Tai page, as read, is silent; the Eastern Wei dossier (Gao Huan page) has Gao Huan's fall 538 siege forcing the Western Wei out of Luoyang.

union.text: the western Henan and southwestern Shanxi lands of the Western Wei shape

region.text: the Luoyang region and the Henan-Shanxi lands west of it, the zone the Eastern Wei dossier fights over in 537-538

ledger.note: 538: the first round ends. The pages opened are silent on how the 537-538 fighting ended; the Eastern Wei dossier ends the Luoyang siege in 538.
543: Hulao comes over. 'In spring 543, the Eastern Wei official Gao Zhongmi... surrendered his headquarters of Hulao' to the Western Wei.

543: the Western Wei are driven off again. The Yuwen Tai page, as read, says no more than the surrender; the Eastern Wei dossier has them repelled the same year. Yubi was besieged by Gao Huan in 546 ('In 546, Gao Huan launched another major attack on Western Wei').

region.text: Xiangyang, the territory Xiao Cha surrendered to the Western Wei

ledger.note: 549: Xiao Cha hands over Xiangyang. 'By winter 549, one of the Liang princes, Xiao Cha the Prince of Yueyang' surrendered the Xiangyang territory; in spring 550 the Western Wei defeated Xiao Yi's general Liu Zhongli. The page does not call it a vassalage.

553: the Western Wei take Sichuan. 'In spring 553, with Xiao Ji and Xiao Yi... Yuwen sent his nephew Yuchi Jiong to attack Xiao Ji's domain'; the Western Wei page: it 'occupied the territory of modern Sichuan' (no year).

553: Hanzhong goes to the Western Wei. The Yuwen Tai page: in summer 552 Xiao Yi 'agreed to cede Nanzheng (modern Hanzhong, Shaanxi) to Western Wei', his cousin Xiao Xun refused, Yuwen Tai and Daxi Wu attacked Hanzhong and after a long siege Xiao Xun surrendered and 'Nanzheng was in Western Wei hands'. The page gives no year for the surrender; 553 follows the Liang dossier. [Reviewer ea-03-f, 2026-10-19: source moved from the Western Wei page to the Yuwen Tai page, which names Nanzheng; confidence raised from 1 to 2]

Infobox 'Established: 555', 'Puppet state of Western Wei, Northern Zhou, and Sui dynasty'; 'In the winter of 554, under Yuwen Tai's orders, Western Wei forces, commanded by Yu Jin, launched the attack' and 'Western Wei created Xiao Cha the Emperor of Liang' (Yuwen Tai page).

wars.name: Western Wei conquest of the western Liang

zones.text: Xiao Ji's Sichuan, Xiangyang and Jiangling

wars.outcome: Western Wei took Xiangyang (549), Sichuan (spring 553) and Jiangling (winter 554), killed Emperor Yuan and set up the puppet Western Liang under Xiao Cha in 555.
wars.note: Hanzhong is not on the page.

certainty.note: The Eastern Wei frontier moved by campaign at Hengnong and Hulao; the Rouran, Tuyuhun and Tujue frontiers are approximate, and no treaty or survey fixes any edge.

notes:
CLIOPATRIA ROW. The row (534-560) ends three years late (557): the 558-560 years are the Northern Zhou's (keyframe northern-zhou_557). The 536 shape adds the Sichuan basin and Hanzhong seventeen years before the pages date them (spring 553), so western-wei_536 is replaced by the 534 shape for 536-548, with Xiangyang added in 549 and Sichuan and Hanzhong in 553. The infobox gives no area, so none of the shapes was compared.
START. The infobox gives two starts: 8 November 534 (the split) and 18 February 535 ('often viewed as establishment'); the dossier uses the first to match Cliopatria and the Northern Wei dossier (ends 534).
NOT ON THE PAGES OPENED. The Western Wei page has almost no events (Shayuan 537 and the Changle marriage); the Yuwen Tai page does not name Hanzhong, Yi Province, the Mangshan or Hengshui battles, or Tuyuhun; Xiao Cha's enthronement year (555) comes from the Western Liang page. The Eastern Wei dossier (another part) carries the 537-538 and 543 Luoyang-region fights; the closing events here are bridged at confidence 1. Bumin Qaghan 'married the Western Wei princess Changle in June 551' and founded the Turkic Khaganate in 552: an alliance, not a vassalage; the Rouran are neighbours.
COUNTERPART NAMES. xiao-ji-s-rebel-state is the existing dossier of Xiao Ji (552-553); the Hanzhong gain's counterpart liang-dynasty follows that dossier's 553 loss.
PAGE BUDGET. Western Wei and Yuwen Tai (two pages) plus the shared Western Liang page.
